newsitem.title: USA: Delta II rocket launch postponed again.
newsitem.headline: Delta II rocket launch postponed again.

text.p: High winds on Saturday forced the U.S. Air Force to postpone for a second time the launch of a Delta II rocket carrying the first five satellites for the IRIDIUM LLC communications project.
A spokeswoman at Vandenberg Air Force Base said a third attempt to launch the rocket had been scheduled for Sunday morning at 8:01 a.m. PDT (11.01 a.m. EDT/1501 GMT).

On Friday, the first scheduled launch was scrubbed because of high-level winds -- at between 20,000 feet and 50,000 feet (6,100 metres and 15,250 metres) -- which Christine Nelson, a spokeswoman for McDonnell Douglas Corp, makers of the rocket, said were "beyond the safety parameters."

The decision to postpone Saturday's launch attempt was made after high winds were detected by a computerized instrument carried into the upper level by a balloon shortly before the scheduled launch time.
The planned launch in southern California is the first of a Delta II rocket since January, when a Delta II exploded shortly after takeoff from Cape Canaveral, Florida.

IRIDIUM is an international consortium of 17 companies, including Motorola Inc, Sprint Corp, Lockheed Martin Corp, Raytheon Co and Pacific Electric Wire & Cable Co Ltd. The largest stakeholder is Motorola, with about 25 percent.
The consortium plans a global telecommunications network using 66 low-orbit satellites.
